name: 1139 Delaware Street (1139 Delaware)
award: 2025 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Sherman Associates and the Denver Housing Authority plan 1139 Delaware, an 80-unit permanent supportive housing building for people exiting homelessness, including people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, with every unit at 30% AMI and backed by project-based vouchers, on DHA land in Denver's Golden Triangle. It won 2025 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits from CHFA, with $20.9M of CHFA bonds.
why_it_matters: It shows the DHA Delivers for Denver (D3) model at work: DHA bought the land with bond money, leases it for $100 a year, provides a property tax exemption and 60 project-based vouchers, and the state adds 20 Section 811 vouchers and a $3.5M Proposition 123 loan. The deal was cut from 132 mixed-income units to 80 PSH units to win credits.

status.label: Credits awarded and Prop 123 loan preliminarily approved; closing and construction not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA reserved the credits in November 2025, and the state preliminarily approved a $3.5M Proposition 123 concessionary loan on 2026-07-21. The project was in Denver concept plan review in early 2026; the application targeted building permits and financial closing in the third quarter of 2026. No public record of a closing, permit or groundbreaking was found.

next_step: Watch for a CHFA bond closing, Denver HOST loan and services agreements at City Council, demolition and building permits, and a groundbreaking.

key_numbers.meaning: 8 studios, 52 one-bedroom, 12 two-bedroom and 8 three-bedroom units for individuals and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness; units come furnished.
About $16.4M over 10 years, plus $1,800,000 accelerated state credit.
60 Housing Choice Vouchers from DHA and 20 Section 811 vouchers from the Colorado Division of Housing.
Preliminarily approved by OEDIT and CHFA in July 2026, with final terms set in underwriting.

background.text: DHA assembled the site and bought it for $5.85 million through its D3 program, which is backed by city bonds; DHA then ran an RFQ and picked Sherman Associates in fall 2023.

The original plan, announced in December 2023, was about 132 units: 80 PSH units plus 52 units at 60% AMI, with groundbreaking as soon as spring 2025 and completion in fall 2026. Denver7 put the cost at about $58 million.

The 132-unit, seven-story version applied for 2024 4% and state credits and was not awarded. It had proposed 40 DHA and 40 DOH vouchers, Capital Magnet Fund money, and volume cap from both Denver and CHFA.
After funder feedback, Sherman cut the project to 80 units, all PSH at 30% AMI, citing the cost and management strain of mixing supportive and general-occupancy housing.

Zoning is in place. The project is in the city's Affordable Housing Review Team program and had received preliminary concept plan comments at application; it was still in concept plan review when Developing MyCity reported in early 2026.
The Phase I found two recognized environmental conditions; a Phase II found no further investigation warranted, and a materials management plan will be followed.
Sherman held community meetings at the Evans School on 2024-02-15 and 2024-02-21 and joined the Golden Triangle Creative District association.
The market analyst expects lease-up of about 15 units a month and notes 3,108 existing PSH units in the market area, with Forum Apartments the closest at 0.3 mile.
The applicant requested a cost basis waiver, citing the small site, podium parking, Davis-Bacon wages and extra services space.

discrepancies.text: DHA's project page still lists 132 units (80 at 30% AMI and 52 at 60% AMI) with completion expected in fall 2026, while CHFA lists 80 units, all at 30% AMI.
The application and Naked Denver describe a five-story building, while Developing MyCity describes six stories.
The award report lists $20,907,615 in bonds, while the application proposed $23,059,433 of construction-period bonds.

Bisnow describes the project as supportive housing for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, while CHFA and the application describe it as housing for people exiting or at risk of homelessness, some of whom may have such disabilities.
Developing MyCity names DHA as owner/developer and Sherman as affordable housing partner/operator, while CHFA names Sherman Associates Development LLC as sponsor.
